title: The Campaign Launch
prompt: Your biggest campaign of the year launches tomorrow. The creative team just flagged a typo in the hero banner that's already been sent to print.

leftChoice.label: Reprint everything
leftChoice.outcomeText: The reprint costs a fortune but the campaign looks flawless. Leadership notices your commitment to quality.

rightChoice.label: Launch as-is
rightChoice.outcomeText: Three people on Twitter spot the typo. It becomes a minor PR moment. Your CMO is not amused.

title: The Agency Pitch
prompt: Two agencies pitched for your brand refresh. One is safe and reliable. The other is bold and risky but could be transformative.

leftChoice.label: Go with the bold agency
leftChoice.outcomeText: The campaign turns heads. It's polarizing but generates massive buzz. Your CMO calls it 'brave.'

rightChoice.label: Go with the safe agency
rightChoice.outcomeText: The campaign is solid and on-brand. No one talks about it much, but nothing goes wrong.

title: The Budget Reallocation
prompt: Q3 results are in. Digital ads are outperforming events. Finance wants you to cut the events budget and double down on digital.

leftChoice.label: Shift budget to digital
leftChoice.outcomeText: ROI improves significantly. The events team is upset but the numbers speak for themselves.

rightChoice.label: Keep the balanced mix
rightChoice.outcomeText: You maintain relationships across channels. Finance questions your data-driven thinking.

title: The Influencer Deal
prompt: A popular influencer with 2M followers wants to partner. Their audience is perfect but their past tweets are... problematic.

leftChoice.label: Pass on the partnership
leftChoice.outcomeText: Two months later the influencer gets cancelled. Your brand is untouched. Good call.

rightChoice.label: Sign the deal
rightChoice.outcomeText: The reach is great initially. Then someone digs up the old tweets. Crisis mode activated.

title: The Viral Moment
prompt: A competitor just had a PR disaster. Your social media manager wants to post a witty jab. It could go viral.

leftChoice.label: Post the jab
leftChoice.outcomeText: The tweet gets 50K likes. The brand feels human and witty. The competitor's PR team is furious.

rightChoice.label: Stay above the fray
rightChoice.outcomeText: You take the high road. The moment passes. Your brand stays classy but misses the cultural moment.

title: The Rebrand Proposal
prompt: The CEO wants a full rebrand — new logo, new colors, new tagline. The timeline is 3 months. It normally takes 12.

leftChoice.label: Commit to the timeline
leftChoice.outcomeText: You pull it off. The rebrand launches on time. It's not perfect but the CEO is thrilled.

rightChoice.label: Push back on the timeline
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CEO is annoyed but agrees to 6 months. The extra time produces a much stronger brand identity.

title: The Trade Show
prompt: The annual industry trade show is next month. A booth costs $50K and requires your whole team for a week.

leftChoice.label: Book the booth
leftChoice.outcomeText: Great leads and brand visibility. The team is exhausted but the pipeline looks healthy.

rightChoice.label: Skip it this year
rightChoice.outcomeText: Competitors dominate the show floor. Sales asks why you weren't there.

title: The Content Calendar
prompt: Your content team is burned out from daily posting. They want to drop to 3x per week. Engagement data says daily posting wins.

leftChoice.label: Maintain daily posting
leftChoice.outcomeText: Engagement stays high. Two content writers quietly start job hunting.

rightChoice.label: Reduce posting frequency
rightChoice.outcomeText: The team is happier. Engagement dips slightly but quality improves noticeably.

title: The PR Crisis
prompt: A journalist is writing a negative piece about your company. They've reached out for comment. You have 2 hours.

leftChoice.label: Engage and provide a statement
leftChoice.outcomeText: Your statement is quoted prominently. The article is still negative but your response looks measured and professional.

rightChoice.label: No comment
rightChoice.outcomeText: The article runs without your side. It looks like you're hiding something.

title: The A/B Test
prompt: Your A/B test results are in. Version B wins by 12% but the CEO prefers Version A aesthetically.

leftChoice.label: Go with Version B (data wins)
leftChoice.outcomeText: Conversions improve. You present the results to the CEO with confidence. They come around.

rightChoice.label: Go with Version A (CEO wins)
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CEO is happy. Performance suffers. Your team loses faith in data-driven decision making.

title: The Brand Guidelines
prompt: Sales keeps using off-brand materials they made themselves. It's inconsistent and hurts brand equity.

leftChoice.label: Enforce brand guidelines strictly
leftChoice.outcomeText: Brand consistency improves. Sales is annoyed but eventually appreciates the polished materials you provide.

rightChoice.label: Let it slide
rightChoice.outcomeText: The brand continues to fragment. A new VP of Sales later asks why the brand looks inconsistent.

title: The Email Blast
prompt: The sales team wants to send a promotional email to your entire 500K subscriber list. Your data shows 40% are disengaged.

leftChoice.label: Send to the full list
leftChoice.outcomeText: Unsubscribe rates spike. Your sender reputation takes a hit. Short-term revenue bump though.

rightChoice.label: Segment and send to engaged users only
rightChoice.outcomeText: Open rates are excellent. Sales grumbles about the smaller send but the metrics look great.

title: The Podcast Sponsorship
prompt: A popular industry podcast is offering a sponsorship slot. The audience is perfect but the cost is 20% of your quarterly budget.

leftChoice.label: Sponsor the podcast
leftChoice.outcomeText: Brand awareness in your target segment jumps. Attribution is hard to prove but the sales team notices more warm leads.

rightChoice.label: Pass — hard to measure ROI
rightChoice.outcomeText: A competitor takes the slot. You keep the budget for performance channels.

title: The Creative Disagreement
prompt: Your creative director and your data analyst are at war. The creative wants bold visuals; the analyst says the data shows minimalism converts better.

leftChoice.label: Side with the creative
leftChoice.outcomeText: The campaign is beautiful. Conversion rates are mediocre. The creative director loves you.

rightChoice.label: Side with the data
rightChoice.outcomeText: Conversions improve. The creative director sulks for a week.

title: The Product Launch Event
prompt: The product team wants a splashy launch event. You have 6 weeks and a modest budget.

leftChoice.label: Go big — rent a venue
leftChoice.outcomeText: The event is spectacular. Press coverage is excellent. You're over budget but the CMO is ecstatic.

rightChoice.label: Do a virtual launch instead
rightChoice.outcomeText: The virtual event is efficient and well-produced. The product team feels it lacked excitement.

title: The SEO vs Paid Debate
prompt: You need to grow web traffic fast. SEO takes 6 months to show results. Paid ads work immediately but stop when the budget runs out.

leftChoice.label: Invest in SEO
leftChoice.outcomeText: Six months later, organic traffic is booming. Leadership questions why it took so long.

rightChoice.label: Run paid campaigns
rightChoice.outcomeText: Traffic spikes immediately. When the budget runs out, so does the traffic.

title: The Competitor's Campaign
prompt: A competitor just launched a campaign that's eerily similar to your upcoming one. You're launching in 2 weeks.

leftChoice.label: Differentiate and pivot
leftChoice.outcomeText: The pivot is stressful but your campaign stands out. No one notices the similarity.

rightChoice.label: Launch as planned
rightChoice.outcomeText: Industry blogs compare the two campaigns. Yours is called 'derivative.' Ouch.

title: The Marketing Attribution
prompt: Sales claims they closed a deal with zero marketing involvement. You have data showing 8 marketing touchpoints before the close.

leftChoice.label: Present the attribution data
leftChoice.outcomeText: The data is compelling. The VP of Sales grudgingly acknowledges marketing's role.

rightChoice.label: Let sales take the credit
rightChoice.outcomeText: Sales is happy. Marketing's budget justification gets harder next quarter.

title: The Social Media Controversy
prompt: One of your brand's social posts is being misinterpreted and getting negative comments. It's gaining momentum.

leftChoice.label: Delete the post and apologize
leftChoice.outcomeText: The apology is well-received. The story dies quickly. Crisis averted.

rightChoice.label: Clarify the intent and stand firm
rightChoice.outcomeText: Some people appreciate the clarity. Others double down. The controversy lingers for days.

title: The Marketing Hire
prompt: You need to hire a new content manager. One candidate has great writing skills but no marketing experience. The other has marketing experience but mediocre writing.

leftChoice.label: Hire the great writer
leftChoice.outcomeText: Content quality soars. You spend months teaching them marketing fundamentals.

rightChoice.label: Hire the marketing experienced
rightChoice.outcomeText: They hit the ground running on strategy. Content quality is consistently mediocre.

title: The Brand Partnership
prompt: A well-known brand in an adjacent category wants to co-market. It's a great audience fit but they want equal billing.

leftChoice.label: Accept the co-marketing deal
leftChoice.outcomeText: The partnership generates significant reach. Both brands benefit. Your CMO calls it a win.

rightChoice.label: Negotiate for top billing
rightChoice.outcomeText: The other brand walks. You lose the partnership over a logo placement dispute.

title: The Marketing Dashboard
prompt: Leadership wants a weekly marketing dashboard. Building it properly takes 2 weeks. A quick version takes 2 hours but will be full of caveats.

leftChoice.label: Build it properly
leftChoice.outcomeText: The dashboard is clean and trusted. Leadership references it in every meeting.

rightChoice.label: Ship the quick version
rightChoice.outcomeText: Leadership uses it but keeps asking questions the dashboard can't answer.

title: The Tone of Voice
prompt: The CEO wants the brand to sound 'more fun and edgy.' Your brand research shows your audience prefers 'professional and trustworthy.'

leftChoice.label: Present the research and push back
leftChoice.outcomeText: The CEO listens to the data. They agree to a subtle refresh rather than a full tone overhaul.

rightChoice.label: Follow the CEO's direction
rightChoice.outcomeText: The new tone confuses your core audience. Engagement drops. The CEO blames the execution.

title: The Customer Case Study
prompt: Your best customer is willing to do a case study. Legal says it'll take 6 weeks of approvals. Sales needs it in 2 weeks.

leftChoice.label: Fast-track through legal
leftChoice.outcomeText: You navigate legal in record time. Sales closes two deals using the case study.

rightChoice.label: Follow the normal process
rightChoice.outcomeText: The case study is perfect when it finally arrives. Sales already closed the deals without it.

title: The Reels Strategy
prompt: Your team wants to go all-in on short-form video. It requires hiring a videographer and completely changing your content mix.

leftChoice.label: Go all-in on video
leftChoice.outcomeText: Your Reels take off. Follower growth is the highest in company history. The investment pays off.

rightChoice.label: Test with existing resources first
rightChoice.outcomeText: The test videos are rough but informative. You learn what works before committing fully.

title: The Quarterly Business Review
prompt: QBR is tomorrow. Your MQL numbers are down but your pipeline quality is up. The story is nuanced.

leftChoice.label: Lead with pipeline quality
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership appreciates the nuanced view. The CFO asks smart follow-up questions. You hold your own.

rightChoice.label: Bury the MQL decline in the slides
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CFO spots it anyway. Being caught hiding bad news is worse than the bad news itself.

title: The Agency Relationship
prompt: Your agency has been underperforming for two quarters. They're a long-standing partner and the CEO plays golf with the agency founder.

leftChoice.label: Put them on a performance plan
leftChoice.outcomeText: The agency steps up. The relationship is tense but the work improves.

rightChoice.label: Let it slide to avoid politics
rightChoice.outcomeText: Performance continues to suffer. Your CMO asks why you haven't addressed it.

title: The Thought Leadership Article
prompt: A top industry publication wants an op-ed from your CMO. They're too busy. They want you to ghostwrite it.

leftChoice.label: Write the article
leftChoice.outcomeText: The article is excellent. The CMO is thrilled. You get zero public credit but significant internal goodwill.

rightChoice.label: Suggest the CMO writes it themselves
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CMO is annoyed. The opportunity passes. The publication fills the slot with a competitor.

title: The Localization Decision
prompt: You're expanding to three new markets. Full localization of all content takes 4 months. Translated-only takes 3 weeks.

leftChoice.label: Full localization
leftChoice.outcomeText: The local markets respond warmly. Culturally resonant content drives strong early adoption.

rightChoice.label: Translation only
rightChoice.outcomeText: The content feels foreign. Local teams complain it doesn't resonate. Adoption is slow.

title: The Webinar Series
prompt: You want to launch a monthly webinar series for lead generation. It requires significant ongoing commitment from your team.

leftChoice.label: Launch the series
leftChoice.outcomeText: The series builds a loyal audience. Lead quality is excellent. Your team is stretched thin.

rightChoice.label: Do one-off webinars instead
rightChoice.outcomeText: One-offs are easier to manage but don't build the same audience loyalty.

title: The Competitive Positioning
prompt: Your competitor just dropped their price by 20%. Your VP of Sales wants marketing to update all messaging to emphasize value over price.

leftChoice.label: Reposition around value
leftChoice.outcomeText: The repositioning is sharp and well-received. Sales has a clear story to tell.

rightChoice.label: Match the price messaging
rightChoice.outcomeText: You enter a race to the bottom. Brand perception suffers.

title: The Marketing Ops Stack
prompt: Your marketing tech stack has 14 tools, many overlapping. Consolidating would save $80K/year but requires 3 months of migration work.

leftChoice.label: Consolidate the stack
leftChoice.outcomeText: The migration is painful but the savings are real. Finance loves you.

rightChoice.label: Keep the status quo
rightChoice.outcomeText: You avoid the migration headache. The redundant tools keep costing money.

title: The Award Submission
prompt: There's an industry award for 'Best Marketing Campaign.' Submitting requires 20 hours of work compiling case studies.

leftChoice.label: Submit for the award
leftChoice.outcomeText: You win! The award generates press coverage and boosts team morale significantly.

rightChoice.label: Skip it — too much effort
rightChoice.outcomeText: A competitor wins the award. Their PR team makes sure everyone knows about it.

title: The Demand Gen vs Brand Debate
prompt: The CFO wants all marketing spend tied to measurable pipeline. Your brand-building budget is under threat.

leftChoice.label: Defend the brand budget
leftChoice.outcomeText: You make a compelling case for long-term brand equity. The CFO cuts it by 30% instead of 100%.

rightChoice.label: Shift everything to demand gen
rightChoice.outcomeText: Short-term pipeline improves. Brand awareness slowly erodes over the next year.

title: The Negative Review
prompt: A scathing G2 review from a churned customer is gaining traction. It's mostly inaccurate but contains a kernel of truth.

leftChoice.label: Respond publicly and address it
leftChoice.outcomeText: Your measured response impresses prospects. Transparency wins.

rightChoice.label: Ignore it
rightChoice.outcomeText: The review sits unanswered. Prospects read it and wonder why no one responded.

title: The Newsletter Growth
prompt: Your newsletter has 10K subscribers. A growth hack could add 5K more but they'd be low-quality leads from a giveaway.

leftChoice.label: Run the giveaway
leftChoice.outcomeText: Subscriber count jumps. Open rates tank. The list is full of people who wanted the free iPad.

rightChoice.label: Grow organically
rightChoice.outcomeText: Growth is slower but every subscriber is genuinely interested. Engagement is excellent.

title: The Sales Enablement Request
prompt: Sales wants 10 new one-pagers, 5 battle cards, and a new pitch deck — all by end of month.

leftChoice.label: Deliver everything
leftChoice.outcomeText: Sales is thrilled. Your team worked nights and weekends. Two people ask about their workload.

rightChoice.label: Prioritize the top 3 items
rightChoice.outcomeText: Sales is disappointed but the three items you deliver are excellent.

title: The Customer Community
prompt: You want to build an online customer community. It's a long-term play with no immediate ROI.

leftChoice.label: Build the community
leftChoice.outcomeText: 18 months later the community is thriving. NPS scores improve. Churn drops. It was worth it.

rightChoice.label: Focus on shorter-term wins
rightChoice.outcomeText: You hit your quarterly targets. The community opportunity passes to a competitor.

title: The Analyst Briefing
prompt: Gartner wants to brief you for their annual Magic Quadrant. It takes 2 days of prep and a full-day session.

leftChoice.label: Invest in the briefing
leftChoice.outcomeText: You're placed as a Visionary. The placement drives significant inbound interest.

rightChoice.label: Send a junior to handle it
rightChoice.outcomeText: The briefing goes poorly. You're placed as a Niche Player. Sales is not happy.

title: The Reactivation Campaign
prompt: You have 50K dormant leads in your CRM. A reactivation campaign could wake some up but risks spam complaints.

leftChoice.label: Run a targeted reactivation
leftChoice.outcomeText: 3% reactivate. That's 1,500 warm leads. Spam complaints are within acceptable limits.

rightChoice.label: Clean the list instead
rightChoice.outcomeText: Your list hygiene improves dramatically. Deliverability scores go up. Sales asks where the leads went.

title: The Sponsorship Request
prompt: A local charity asks your brand to sponsor their gala. The CEO is on their board.

leftChoice.label: Sponsor the gala
leftChoice.outcomeText: The CEO is pleased. The brand gets good local press. The ROI is impossible to measure.

rightChoice.label: Decline — not in the budget
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CEO notices. You get a subtle reminder about 'community investment' in the next all-hands.

title: The Marketing Intern
prompt: Your summer intern produced a campaign idea that's genuinely brilliant. Better than most of your team's ideas.

leftChoice.label: Champion the idea with full credit to them
leftChoice.outcomeText: The intern is thrilled. The team respects your integrity. The campaign performs well.

rightChoice.label: Refine it and present it as a team effort
rightChoice.outcomeText: The campaign succeeds. The intern knows what happened. Word gets around.

title: The Persona Research
prompt: Your buyer personas are 3 years old. Refreshing them requires 6 weeks of customer interviews and surveys.

leftChoice.label: Refresh the personas
leftChoice.outcomeText: The new personas reveal a completely different buyer profile. All your messaging needs updating. Worth it.

rightChoice.label: Use the existing personas
rightChoice.outcomeText: You keep shipping campaigns. They feel slightly off but no one can articulate why.

title: The Viral Video
prompt: Your team produced a quirky video that's getting organic traction. It's off-brand but the engagement is incredible.

leftChoice.label: Boost it with paid spend
leftChoice.outcomeText: The video reaches 2M views. Brand awareness spikes. The CMO asks if it was intentional.

rightChoice.label: Let it ride organically
rightChoice.outcomeText: It peaks at 200K views. A missed opportunity to amplify, but the brand stays consistent.

title: The CMO Presentation
prompt: Your CMO asks you to present the marketing strategy to the board next week. It's a huge opportunity but also a huge risk.

leftChoice.label: Accept and prepare thoroughly
leftChoice.outcomeText: The board is impressed. The CMO looks great for developing you. You're now on the board's radar.

rightChoice.label: Suggest the CMO presents instead
rightChoice.outcomeText: The CMO is surprised. They present it themselves. The opportunity to shine passes.

title: The Retargeting Campaign
prompt: Your retargeting ads are following users too aggressively. Conversion is up but brand sentiment surveys show people find it 'creepy.'

leftChoice.label: Dial back the frequency
leftChoice.outcomeText: Sentiment improves. Conversions dip slightly but the brand feels less predatory.

rightChoice.label: Keep the aggressive targeting
rightChoice.outcomeText: Conversions stay high. A tech journalist writes a piece about 'creepy ad stalking.' Your brand is mentioned.

title: The Campaign Post-Mortem
prompt: The last campaign underperformed. Your team is demoralized. Leadership wants to know what went wrong.

leftChoice.label: Present an honest post-mortem
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership respects the transparency. The learnings improve the next campaign significantly.

rightChoice.label: Blame external factors
rightChoice.outcomeText: Leadership sees through it. Trust erodes. The same mistakes repeat next quarter.

title: The Marketing Offsite
prompt: You want to take the team on a 2-day offsite for strategy and team building. Finance says it's a luxury.

leftChoice.label: Fight for the offsite
leftChoice.outcomeText: The offsite is energizing. Team cohesion improves noticeably. Finance grumbles about the cost.

rightChoice.label: Do a virtual strategy day instead
rightChoice.outcomeText: The virtual day is fine. The team misses the in-person energy.

title: The Product-Marketing Misalignment
prompt: Product is launching a feature next week that marketing hasn't been briefed on. There's no time for a proper go-to-market.

leftChoice.label: Delay the launch
leftChoice.outcomeText: The extra week produces a much stronger launch. Product is annoyed but the results justify it.

rightChoice.label: Launch with a minimal announcement
rightChoice.outcomeText: The feature launches quietly. Customers barely notice. A great feature goes unappreciated.

title: The Marketing Budget Cut
prompt: Finance just cut your marketing budget by 25% mid-year. You need to decide what to cut.

leftChoice.label: Cut brand, protect demand gen
leftChoice.outcomeText: Pipeline stays healthy short-term. Brand awareness slowly declines over the next two quarters.

rightChoice.label: Cut evenly across all channels
rightChoice.outcomeText: Everything gets slightly worse but nothing collapses. A balanced approach in a tough situation.
